source.version: Undated manuscript PDF on file; no journal publication details, date, or version identifier are printed on the title page (p. 1). The exact arXiv version cannot be confirmed from this document.
source.title_on_document: Epitome: Pioneering an Experimental Platform for AI-Social Science Integration

supplement.where: Separate Supplementary Information is cited on pp. 10, 12 and 18. The data-availability statement points to https://github.com/epitome-AISS/epitome for further information, without a direct supplement-file link (p. 18). A Nature Research Reporting Summary is also mentioned without an actionable link in this PDF (p. 16).
supplement.holds: The paper says detailed case-study data and experimental materials are in Supplementary Information (p. 18). It cites Supplementary Figure 10 for writing output quality, Figures 9 and 11-13 for completion time and participant-reported outcomes (p. 10), Figures 21-22 for creativity results, Tables 2-3 and Figure 33 for moral-reasoning results (p. 12), and Section G for the platform manual (p. 18). These materials are absent from the supplied PDF; their participant counts, arm statistics and standard errors cannot be verified.

paper_design_summary: The platform paper reports three case studies: managers assigned to ChatGPT or Overleaf for incentivized writing, story writers randomly assigned zero, one or five AI ideas, and moral-reasoning simulations involving AI agents and human participants (pp. 9-13). Experts scored writing quality, content quality and originality in the writing studies; the text also reports summary output quality, individual creativity and collective diversity (pp. 9-12). The professional-writing study analyzed 35 people, while the story-writing participant count is unstated and its figure labels 31 stories (p. 9, Fig. 2; p. 11, Fig. 3a).

studies.label: Case Study 1: professional writing (Noy and Zhang replication)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Managers were allocated to ChatGPT versus Overleaf through the Random Design module (p. 10). Fig. 2a shows a common Task 1 before tool sign-up and a Task 2 after sign-up; the caption describes two incentivized tasks and training on the respective tools (p. 9). Between-person tool assignment is combined with repeated writing tasks; the main text does not specify the statistical model for this structure.

arms.name: Overleaf

The exact task prompts are not specified in the main text (p. 9, Fig. 2a and caption). Originality is an output criterion, supporting inclusion of the writing outcomes in this screening.

studies.label: Case Study 2: adventure stories, English and Chinese conditions (Doshi and Hauser replication)

assignment.what_was_assigned: People were randomly assigned to Human-only, one AI-generated suggestion, or five AI-generated suggestions for story writing (p. 11, Fig. 3 caption). The text explicitly describes a between-subjects design (p. 10). Assignment to language conditions and whether languages used independent participant samples are not stated.
assignment.quote: In this experiment, participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups: a control group (Human-only), a group with one AI-generated suggestion, and a group with five AI-generated suggestions.
assignment.locator: p. 11, Fig. 3 caption; p. 10, Human creativity and generative AI.

arms.name: Human-only
arms.description: Story writing without AI-generated suggestions (p. 11, Fig. 3 caption).

arms.name: One AI-generated suggestion
arms.description: Story writing with one AI-generated suggestion; the workflow limits the number of ideas supplied (p. 11, Fig. 3 caption).

arms.name: Five AI-generated suggestions
arms.description: Story writing with five AI-generated suggestions; the workflow limits the number of ideas supplied (p. 11, Fig. 3 caption).

participants.exclusions: Participant recruitment, exclusions, total people, and people per arm or language are not stated in the supplied PDF (pp. 10-12). Fig. 3a labels 31 stories, an output count, not a stated participant count. Neither that label nor the reported test degrees of freedom establishes how many people were analyzed.
participants.who: Human participants writing adventure stories; demographic and recruitment details are not reported (pp. 10-12).
participants.locator: p. 11, Fig. 3a, label on the arrow leading to expert evaluation; pp. 10-12, Human creativity and generative AI and Fig. 3 caption.

ai_tool.how_used: Two AI advisors were configured using prompts and model parameters, and a Dify-based workflow limited and distributed one or five AI ideas in a one-to-one environment (pp. 10-11, Human creativity and generative AI; Fig. 3 caption). The particular model and version are not identified. Suggestions were provided for the story being evaluated, not solely for an earlier practice task.

task.description: Write an adventure story with zero, one or five AI suggestions; experts then evaluate the stories. A Chinese condition was added to assess cross-cultural generalizability, and the results refer to English and Chinese conditions (p. 11, Fig. 3 caption; p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI).

outcomes.name: Individual creativity (reported summary score)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Stories undergo expert evaluation for writing quality, content quality and originality (p. 11, Fig. 3 caption). The reported individual-creativity score is not operationally defined or mapped to these dimensions; its scale, rating aggregation, and statistical observation unit are not stated (p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI). The text says gains are particularly pronounced for lower-baseline creators and consistent across English and Chinese conditions, without subgroup or language-specific numerical contrasts. Supplementary Figures 21-22 are cited but absent. The 31 stories shown in Fig. 3a are not identified as the observations behind the reported tests, so n_units for this summary result is null.

contrasts.reported: Individual creativity increasing by 42.1% with 1 AI idea (T-test result: t = 5.30, p < 0.01, df = 149). Arm means, SDs, SEs and confidence intervals are not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI, first paragraph; cites Supplementary Figure 21-22 (not in this PDF).

contrasts.reported: Individual creativity increasing by 16.4% with 5 AI ideas (T-test result: t = 2.52, p < 0.05, df = 149). Arm means, SDs, SEs and confidence intervals are not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI, first paragraph; cites Supplementary Figure 21-22 (not in this PDF).

outcomes.name: Collective diversity of stories
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: The paper reports convergence of stories and a decline in collective diversity in the baseline replication using standard prompts (p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI). The metric, scoring method, embedding model, scale, observation unit, and arm-specific levels are not described. English and Chinese findings are described jointly. The single contrast below preserves the joint narrative; it is not a computed pooled contrast and does not allocate the reported range or tests to particular AI arms or languages.

contrasts.treatment_arm: One AI-generated suggestion / Five AI-generated suggestions (joint narrative; individual test mapping not stated)
contrasts.reported: Collective diversity decreased by 5.64%-6.47% as outputs converged (T-test result: t = 5.52; T-test result: t = 54.80, p < 0.05, df = 28). The paper does not identify which percentage or test belongs to which AI arm or language, and does not separately print a p value or df beside t = 5.52.
contrasts.locator: p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI, first paragraph, sentence beginning In our baseline replication using standard prompts.

studies.label: Case Study 3: Heinz Dilemma and human-AI courtroom simulations

assignment.what_was_assigned: The authors configured AI characters for a town simulation, then used these agents in courtroom simulations with human participants (pp. 12-13). Random assignment of people to AI assistance versus another condition is not reported. These are phases of one reported case study, not documented randomized assistance arms.
assignment.quote: Phase two deployed these agents in courtroom simulations with human participants
assignment.locator: p. 12, Moral reasoning in human-AI interactions; p. 13, Fig. 4 caption.

participants.exclusions: Not stated. The seven characters in the first phase are AI agents, not people (pp. 12-13). No human sample size is given, and the moral-reasoning test degrees of freedom are not converted into a participant count.
participants.who: Human participants interacted with AI agents in courtroom roles such as judges, jurors and witnesses; recruitment and demographics are not stated (p. 13, Fig. 4 caption).
participants.quote: human participants interacted with AI agents in roles such as judges, jurors, and witnesses.
participants.locator: p. 13, Fig. 4 caption; p. 12, Moral reasoning in human-AI interactions.

ai_tool.how_used: Role-playing language agents interacted in Epitome AI Town and in a human-AI courtroom chatroom (pp. 12-13, Moral reasoning in human-AI interactions; Fig. 4). Model identity is not stated.

task.description: Moral reasoning about Heinz stealing medicine for his wife, first in an AI town and then in a courtroom with human participants. Outcomes concern justice versus care ethics, sentiment, verdicts and leniency; no creative-output or across-writer diversity measure is reported (pp. 12-14; Fig. 4).

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: No reuse of participants from another paper is stated. Case Studies 1 and 2 are described as replications implemented on Epitome of Noy and Zhang and of Doshi and Hauser, respectively, rather than reanalyses of those papers' participants (p. 10). Possible overlap among this paper's case studies or language conditions is not reported.
sample_overlap.quote: We replicated Doshi and Hauser’s study on AI’s impact on creative diversity
sample_overlap.locator: p. 10, Productivity effects of generative AI and Human creativity and generative AI.

company_involvement.description: No commercial-company involvement is reported in the supplied PDF. Listed author affiliations are universities and research institutes; Epitome is the authors' platform. Use of ChatGPT is reported as an intervention, without a stated company research partnership.
company_involvement.locator: p. 1, author affiliations and abstract; pp. 9-10, Case Study 1.

eligibility.reason: Case Study 2 explicitly randomizes people to zero, one or five AI suggestions for adventure-story writing, and experts score their actual stories; collective diversity is also reported (p. 11, Fig. 3 caption; p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI). Its analyzed human sample size is not stated, so the at-least-50 criterion cannot be confirmed. The 31 stories shown in Fig. 3a are outputs, and df = 149 or df = 28 on p. 12 cannot establish participant counts. Case Study 1 has only 35 analyzed people and therefore fails the size criterion (p. 9, Fig. 2 caption). Case Study 3 reports moral reasoning, not a qualifying creative-output outcome (pp. 12-14, Fig. 4). The separate supplementary material needed to resolve the missing counts and analysis details is absent (p. 18, Data, Materials, Software Availability).

one_line_finding: The story-writing replication reports individual creativity gains of 42.1% with one AI idea and 16.4% with five, alongside a 5.64%-6.47% decrease in collective diversity, but does not state the analyzed human sample size (p. 12; p. 11, Fig. 3).
open_questions: What are the numbers of people randomized and analyzed in Case Study 2, including exclusions, arm sizes and language-specific samples, and how do they relate to the 31 stories in Fig. 3a (p. 11)?
What observation units, rating aggregation and dependence adjustments produced the creativity tests with df = 149 and the diversity result with df = 28 (p. 12)?
How are individual creativity and collective diversity defined, and which diversity percentage and test belongs to which AI arm and language (p. 12)?

Do the named writing quality, content quality and originality dimensions have separate results, or are the reported summary quality and creativity scores composites or alternative names for one of them (pp. 9-12)?
Can the Supplementary Information and Reporting Summary be obtained to verify sample sizes, model identities, outcome scales and uncertainty (pp. 16 and 18)?
For Case Study 1, how do the shared Task 1 and post-sign-up Task 2 in Fig. 2a enter the reported quality analysis, and what are the analyzed arm counts (pp. 9-10)?
What dated/versioned manuscript corresponds to this undated saved PDF, whose title page does not identify an arXiv version or publication status (p. 1)?
notes: Screened by B on 2026-10-09. Locators use one-based PDF page indices because the pages are not visibly numbered. The entire markdown conversion, including all references, was read; all six main figures were inspected in the PDF. The supplied PDF ends with references and contains neither the cited Supplementary Information nor an appended Reporting Summary. Figure inventory: Fig. 1 describes platform structure and usage, not eligible creative outcomes; Fig. 2 names writing quality, content quality and originality; Fig. 3 names the same dimensions and identifies individual creativity and collective diversity as targets; Fig. 4 concerns moral reasoning; Figs. 5-6 describe the software. The text additionally reports summary output quality and individual creativity, retained separately because their mapping to the named dimensions is undefined. These entries must not be treated as independent effects without that mapping. Completion time, self-efficacy, task enjoyment and perceptions of AI (p. 10) are outside the output-based creativity questions, as are justice orientation, sentiment, verdicts and leniency (p. 12); they are not counted in outcomes. Case Study 3 is retained to inventory the paper but has no eligible outcomes. The English and Chinese story conditions remain in one study entry because the paper reports them as one case and does not document separate samples. The 31 in S2-O3 through S2-O5 is the same story corpus shown in Fig. 3a, not three samples and not 31 people; these entries identify scored outputs, while the statistical units for the numerical results remain null. The writing experiments are coded online_rct for their implementation through Epitome's web environment (pp. 7 and 16); recruitment panels and physical participation settings are not specified. Overleaf is coded as an active alternative aid because the caption describes tool use and matched training (p. 9). AI availability and immediate timing refer to production of the assisted writing, not the later expert evaluation; no unassisted post-AI transfer output is reported. The GitHub link is the repository named on p. 18; no separate dataset URL is given. No effect sizes, excluded-person counts, or sample sizes were calculated from the printed statistics.
